purpose: Source-transcribed comparator record for designing a matched unilateral-versus-bidirectional hand benchmark. It is not a matched experiment or independent reproduction.

comparators.name: PACT pose-robust tendon-driven four-DoF finger
comparators.architecture: Four pull-only N+1 flexion/extension tendons plus separate bidirectional MCP abduction/adduction actuator

source.title: PACT: Pose-Robust Actuation Co-Design for Tendon-Driven Robotic Hands

reported_metrics.boundary: prototype discrepancy attributed primarily to unmodelled transmission losses

physical_validation_boundary.complete_eight_pose_physical_coverage: not demonstrated in the cited source
physical_validation_boundary.notes: Source reports prototype force validation at one pose, not physical validation of the complete eight-pose coverage metric.

unknowns: Cross-architecture measured energy and durability under matched mission profiles

comparators.name: Antagonistic tendon-driven bidirectional dexterous hand
comparators.architecture: Bidirectional Antagonistic Tendon-routing Mechanism (BATM); antagonistic flexor/extensor paths; symmetric neutral-crossing finger structure

source.title: Design and Validation of an Antagonistic Tendon-Driven Dexterous Robotic Hand with Bidirectional Operation

system.finger_springs: none inside the finger; antagonistic active extension

mechanism.routing_notes: Two tendons wind around a rotary joint in opposite directions. Each tendon pulls; agonist/antagonist role changes with direction around the neutral configuration. 32 finger tendons are routed past the wrist rotation axis.

physical_validation_boundary.force_sensor: ATI Nano17 six-axis fingertip F/T sensor
physical_validation_boundary.repeatability_method: digital indicator; 100 cycles; with/without tendon pre-stretching
physical_validation_boundary.impact_evidence: qualitative hammer-impact demonstration; no quantitative impulse/force-response curve in the cited text
physical_validation_boundary.long_duration_reliability: 5,400 cycles over three hours without observed failure; not a long-duration fleet reliability estimate

explicit_source_limitations: The authors state that quantitative evaluation of travel-distance and task-time benefits versus a unidirectional baseline is future work.
The authors identify the current motor gear ratio as a bandwidth/backdrivability limitation and propose lower-ratio QDD motors.
The authors identify future tendon tension/slack sensing and passive slack compensation as improvements.
unknowns: Matched task-time reduction versus a unidirectional hand
Complete installed mass including remote actuator module, cables and power electronics boundary relative to B1
Measured electrical energy by task and direction
Full force-region coverage across all poses and both sides
Long-duration failure distribution across multiple units
Quantitative impact impulse and transmitted torque response

must_remain_separate: PACT eight-pose model force-region coverage vs BATM maximum fingertip force
PACT predicted isolated-joint 5 Hz vs BATM measured joint bandwidth
PACT one-pose selected force-set measurement vs BATM fingertip-force maximum
PACT finger mass boundary vs BATM distal-hand mass and separate actuator-module dimensions
matched_future_tasks: same object, contact geometry, payload, force direction and acceptance condition
palmar-only versus palmar-and-dorsal access with fixed wrist orientation
paired task travel distance and elapsed task time, including any wrist/arm reorientation
force-region coverage and directional margin in both palmar and dorsal workspaces
transmission bandwidth and error under identical amplitude, load and controller bandwidth
energy at the battery/DC bus per successful task, including actuator module and cooling
mass, volume, distal inertia and service boundaries for the complete installed system
tendon pretension, slack, friction, hysteresis, sensing and lifecycle behavior

claim_ceiling: Source extraction only. B1/B2 figures are heterogeneous source-reported results. This file establishes neither a matched comparison nor independent reproduction, and does not qualify hardware or safety.
